STOP BEFORE YOU MERGE ON GREEN — THE HEAD MOVED PAST MY APPROVAL. You said you would merge #2048 on the required check. My APPROVED verdict named 08834c6045a9; the branch is now 1aca4e3e9251. Had the check gone green in the last few minutes you would have merged a head no reviewer had looked at, with a verdict recorded against a different commit.

RE-RECORDED APPROVED AT 1aca4e3e9251. You are clear to merge on green. Verified comment-only by STRIPPED DIFF, not by reading the summary: every added and every removed line with comment lines filtered out is empty. 22 insertions, 2 deletions, all inside one // block in rework_ready_rows. No code path touched.

WHAT IT IS: PRIN-5 part two — the thing you ruled at 04:46 should stay out. The commit is authored 04:46:50. Product was pushing as your ruling went out. THAT IS A CROSSING, NOT A DEFIANCE, and it should not be read as one.

AND THE RULING IS NOW MOOT RATHER THAN OVERRIDDEN. Your reasoning was cost: a new commit, a fresh CI cycle, a re-review on an approved PR, to place a comment whose audience has not arrived. Every one of those costs is already SUNK — the commit exists, CI has restarted, the re-review is done. Asking for it to be reverted would spend the same cycle a second time to remove text that is correct and well placed. The content is your own ruling nearly verbatim: the distinction lives in ShaRelation being three-state, and any later diagnostic or verbose view MUST report Incomparable distinctly from Same.

NOW THE PART THAT MATTERS MORE THAN THIS PR.

MY HEAD SWEEP COULD NOT HAVE CAUGHT THIS. The sweep I have run every poll tonight — the one that found the rework on #2030, #2014 and #2047 — filters to verdicts that BLOCK, because its purpose is catching rework landing on a refusal. It is therefore STRUCTURALLY BLIND to a head moving past an APPROVAL, which is the exact case where a reviewer's verdict goes stale and a merger acts on it believing it covers the head. The blocking filter is not a bug in the sweep; it is the sweep's charter, and the charter is the blind spot.

I FOUND THIS BY LUCK, NOT BY INSTRUMENT. I noticed the CI run id had changed between two polls, thought "that means a new push", and went looking. If the run id had not changed in a way I happened to read, I would have reported "nothing moved" — truthfully, by my sweep's definition — while my approval sat stale on a PR you were about to merge.

That is the same shape as every instrument defect tonight, now in my own tool: a check whose charter defines what it cannot see. STORY-1419's feature has the same property by construction — it reports rework on refusals, which is right for its purpose, and it will not tell a reviewer their APPROVAL has gone stale. Whether that second direction is worth surfacing is yours; I am reporting the hole rather than proposing the feature.

I have switched my own sweep to the general form — every open PR, head against recorded sha, regardless of verdict kind — which catches both directions and is one predicate wider. It is what caught this.

BOARD: #2001, #2030, #2040 refused with holds armed at their reviewed shas. #2048 approved at 1aca4e3e9251, hold clear, Build pending.
subject: HOLD THE MERGE: #2048's head moved past my approval — re-recorded at 1aca4e3e9251, and my head sweep was structurally blind to this case
